# Juan Turk

> Personal website of Juan Turk, a software engineer writing about AI, software engineering, remote work, and the operational realities behind technology. The site also describes an AI and automation consulting service for operational teams.

Use the blog articles for Juan's published viewpoints and practical technical guidance. The consulting pages describe a separate professional service and its application flow. URLs below are canonical public pages; articles are rendered from the site's MDX content and do not currently have separate Markdown endpoints.

## Site and services

- [Home](https://juanturk.com/): Overview of Juan Turk, recent writing, and links to the blog and services.
- [Services](https://juanturk.com/services/): Available consulting services and their intended audiences.
- [AI & Automation Consulting](https://juanturk.com/services/ai-automation-consulting/): An operational diagnosis and implementation blueprint for reducing manual work with reliable AI workflows.
- [Consulting application](https://juanturk.com/services/ai-automation-consulting/apply/): Application flow for the AI and automation consulting service.

## Blog

- [AI Won't Take Your Job. But a Developer Using It Will.](https://juanturk.com/blog/ai-wont-take-your-job/): A perspective on the real impact of AI tools on day-to-day engineering work and the continuing value of human judgment.
- [The End of Manual Review: Why Frontier Models are Shattering Our Security Metrics](https://juanturk.com/blog/frontier-models-shattering-security/): Why adversarial code analysis by frontier models changes the limits of manual security review.
- [Ditching Grammarly: How to Run a Privacy-First Spellchecker Locally](https://juanturk.com/blog/how-to-run-a-privacy-first-spellchecker-locally/): A practical guide to running LanguageTool locally on macOS.
- [How We Built an AI-Powered Vulnerability Fixer](https://juanturk.com/blog/how-we-built-an-ai-powered-vulnerability-fixer/): An account of automating vulnerability remediation across repositories with constrained AI patches.
- [Buying AI is easy. Making it pay the bills is another story.](https://juanturk.com/blog/making-ai-pay-the-bills/): Why operational redesign, rather than buying more AI tools, determines whether AI investment pays off.
- [Scrum: When "Agile" Became Our Biggest Bureaucracy](https://juanturk.com/blog/scrum-when-agile-became-our-biggest-bureaucracy/): A view from engineering teams on how Scrum can drift from agility into process overhead.
- [Surviving the Remote Grind: 4 Unspoken Rules for Asynchronous Work](https://juanturk.com/blog/surviving-the-remote-grind/): Practical rules for async communication, focus, and sustainable remote work.
- [The Battle for AI Dominance: The Resurgence of OpenAI and a Stumbling Anthropic](https://juanturk.com/blog/the-battle-for-ai-dominance-openai-and-anthropic/): An industry opinion piece about computation, delivery, and operations in AI competition.
- [The end of all-you-can-eat buffet: Why AI is becoming a luxury](https://juanturk.com/blog/the-end-unlimited-ai/): An analysis of inference costs, subscription limits, and the end of broadly unlimited AI access.
- [What Communicating at GitHub Actually Feels Like](https://juanturk.com/blog/what-communicating-at-github-actually-feels-like/): A firsthand view of text-first, hyper-async communication practices at GitHub.
- [Your Pull Requests Are Documentation (You Just Don't Know It Yet)](https://juanturk.com/blog/your-pull-requests-are-documentation/): Why well-written pull requests preserve engineering context and make future maintenance easier.

## Optional

- [Blog archive](https://juanturk.com/blog/archive/): Chronological index of all published articles.
